title: Complete weighted Taylor coefficient model for holomorphic germs
statement:
For $d\geq0$, let $G_d$ be the complex algebra of germs at $0\in\mathbf C^d$ of functions locally represented by convergent complex power series, two representatives agreeing when they agree on a neighbourhood of zero; its operations are pointwise [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations]. For a vector $\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_d)$ of positive real numbers, put $\rho^\alpha=\prod_i\rho_i^{\alpha_i}$ for $\alpha\in\mathbf N^d$ and define
$$A_\rho=\left\{c:\mathbf N^d\to\mathbf C:\ \|c\|_\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbf N^d}|c_\alpha|\rho^\alpha<\infty\right\}.$$
With coefficientwise addition and scalar multiplication, and convolution $(cb)_\alpha=\sum_{\beta+\gamma=\alpha}c_\beta b_\gamma$, this is a complete normed unital complex algebra, with $\|cb\|_\rho\leq\|c\|_\rho\|b\|_\rho$ and unit the coefficient family supported at $\alpha=0$. Complete means that every Cauchy sequence for this norm converges in $A_\rho$. The series $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^\alpha$, where $x^\alpha=\prod_i x_i^{\alpha_i}$, converges absolutely on $|x_i|<\rho_i$ and is holomorphic there in the power-series sense. Sending $c$ to its germ gives an injective complex algebra homomorphism $\gamma_\rho:A_\rho\to G_d$. Every germ in $G_d$ belongs to the image of $\gamma_\rho$ for some positive $\rho$. For $0<\sigma_i\leq\rho_i$, keeping the same coefficients defines $A_\rho\to A_\sigma$, satisfies $\|c\|_\sigma\leq\|c\|_\rho$, and commutes with $\gamma$. Restriction of $\gamma_\rho(c)$ to a coordinate subspace obtained by setting some coordinates to zero keeps precisely the coefficients whose corresponding exponents are zero. For $d=0$, $A_\rho=G_0=\mathbf C$.

The complete weighted coefficient-space formulation is agent supplied, not a verbatim theorem of the source.

proof.text: If $d=0$, the index set $\mathbf N^0$ is a singleton and its unique weight is the empty product $1$. Thus $A_\rho=\mathbf C$ with its absolute-value norm and ordinary product. The space $\mathbf C^0$ is a point, so $G_0=\mathbf C$ and $\gamma_\rho$ is the identity. All restriction and radius assertions then hold. The arguments below also allow empty coordinate sets.

proof.text: Put $I=\mathbf N^d$ and $w_\alpha=\rho^\alpha>0$. The map $T(c)_\alpha=w_\alpha c_\alpha$ is a complex-linear bijection $A_\rho\to\ell^1(I,\mathbf C)$: its inverse divides each coordinate by $w_\alpha$. Moreover $\|T(c)\|_1=\sum_\alpha|c_\alpha|w_\alpha=\|c\|_\rho$. Apply [lem-sfb-complex-l1-completeness] to transport the normed vector-space structure and completeness. Explicitly, a Cauchy sequence $c_n$ gives the Cauchy sequence $T(c_n)$ with limit $u\in\ell^1$; then $T^{-1}u\in A_\rho$ and $\|c_n-T^{-1}u\|_\rho=\|T(c_n)-u\|_1\to0$.

proof.text: For each $\alpha$, the decompositions $\beta+\eta=\alpha$ form a finite set: each $\beta_i$ lies between $0$ and $\alpha_i$ and $\eta=\alpha-\beta$. Also $w_{\beta+\eta}=w_\beta w_\eta$. Let $U_\beta=|c_\beta|w_\beta$ and $V_\eta=|b_\eta|w_\eta$. The product lemma [lem-sfb-absolute-series-product] over $\mathbf R$ shows that the nonnegative family $U_\beta V_\eta$ has sum $\|c\|_\rho\|b\|_\rho$. Group it along $(\beta,\eta)\mapsto\beta+\eta$ using [lem-wf-summable-family-regrouping]. Its grouped family $M_\alpha$ is summable with that sum. The finite triangle inequality gives $|(cb)_\alpha|w_\alpha\leq M_\alpha$. Domination [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] now proves $cb\in A_\rho$ and $\|cb\|_\rho\leq\|c\|_\rho\|b\|_\rho$.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A10_0.pdf, Frenkel exp.10 section 4 printed pp.6-7. Agent-written complete l1 formulation and explicit majorant argument.

proof.text: Each coefficient of a triple product is the same finite sum over $\beta+\eta+\theta=\alpha$, so multiplication is associative; swapping $\beta,\eta$ proves commutativity. Distributivity and compatibility with complex scalars follow by distributing each finite coefficient sum. The family $e_0$ which is $1$ at zero and $0$ elsewhere is the unit and has norm $1$; scalar constants are $\lambda e_0$. Together with the preceding normed-space structure and product estimate this is a normed unital complex algebra. In particular multiplication is continuous: $\|cb-c'b'\|\leq\|c-c'\|\|b\|+\|c'\|\|b-b'\|$, and convergent $c'$ are norm-bounded.

proof.text: For $|z_i|\leq\rho_i$ one has $|c_\alpha z^\alpha|\leq|c_\alpha|\rho^\alpha$. Domination [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] therefore gives absolute convergence of $F_c(z)=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha z^\alpha$, in particular on the required open polydisc. We next verify local power-series representations at every interior point, rather than infer holomorphy merely from convergence at zero.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A10_0.pdf, Frenkel exp.10 section 4 printed pp.6-7. Agent-written complete l1 formulation and explicit majorant argument.

proof.text: Fix an interior point $a$ and choose $t_i>0$ with $|a_i|+t_i<\rho_i$. For pairs $(\beta,\alpha)$ with $\alpha\leq\beta$, set $H_{\beta,\alpha}=|c_\beta|\binom\beta\alpha |a|^{\beta-\alpha}t^\alpha$, using products of coordinate binomial coefficients and $0^0=1$. Every finite subsum of this nonnegative family is at most $\sum_\beta |c_\beta|(|a|+t)^\beta\leq\|c\|_\rho$: enlarge the inner finite sum to all $\alpha\leq\beta$ and use the finite binomial formula in each coordinate. Bounded finite subsums [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] give summability of $H$ and sum at most $\|c\|_\rho$.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A10_0.pdf, Frenkel exp.10 section 4 printed pp.6-7. Agent-written complete l1 formulation and explicit majorant argument.

proof.text: Define $b_\alpha=\sum_{\beta\geq\alpha}c_\beta\binom\beta\alpha a^{\beta-\alpha}$. These sums exist absolutely because the corresponding subfamily of $H$ is summable and $t^\alpha>0$. Group $H$ by $\alpha$ using [lem-wf-summable-family-regrouping] and apply [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] to obtain $\sum_\alpha |b_\alpha|t^\alpha\leq\|c\|_\rho$. For $|h_i|<t_i$, the complex family $c_\beta\binom\beta\alpha a^{\beta-\alpha}h^\alpha$ is absolutely dominated by $H$. Grouping first by $\beta$ gives $F_c(a+h)$ by the finite binomial identity, and grouping first by $\alpha$ gives $\sum_\alpha b_\alpha h^\alpha$. Hence these values agree. This is an absolutely convergent power-series representation on a neighbourhood of $a$, so $F_c$ is holomorphic in the stipulated sense.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A10_0.pdf, Frenkel exp.10 section 4 printed pp.6-7. Agent-written complete l1 formulation and explicit majorant argument.

proof.text: The holomorphic function $F_c$ defines $\gamma_\rho(c)\in G_d$. The pointwise germ operations exist by [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations]. Finite sums give $F_{c+b}=F_c+F_b$, $F_{\lambda c}=\lambda F_c$ and $F_{e_0}=1$. For $z$ in the open polydisc, [lem-sfb-absolute-series-product] applied over $\mathbf C$ to $(c_\beta z^\beta)_\beta$ and $(b_\eta z^\eta)_\eta$ identifies their product with the sum over pairs. Group by $\beta+\eta$ using [lem-wf-summable-family-regrouping]; the finite inner sum is $(cb)_\alpha z^\alpha$. Thus $F_cF_b=F_{cb}$. Passing to germs proves that $\gamma_\rho$ is a unital complex algebra homomorphism.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A10_0.pdf, Frenkel exp.10 section 4 printed pp.6-7. Agent-written complete l1 formulation and explicit majorant argument.

proof.text: Suppose $\gamma_\rho(c)=\gamma_\rho(b)$. The representatives $F_c,F_b$ agree on a neighbourhood of zero, so all their iterated coordinate derivatives at zero agree: difference quotients of equal local functions agree, and this remains true after each differentiation on that neighbourhood. Apply [lem-sfb-monomial-series-coordinate-derivatives] to the summable coefficient families $c$ and $b$. For every $\alpha$ it yields $\alpha!c_\alpha=\partial^\alpha F_c(0)=\partial^\alpha F_b(0)=\alpha!b_\alpha$. The complex number $\alpha!$ is nonzero; cancel it. Thus $c=b$, proving injectivity.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A10_0.pdf, Frenkel exp.10 section 4 printed pp.6-7. Agent-written complete l1 formulation and explicit majorant argument.

proof.text: By the definition of $G_d$, any of its germs has a representative near zero given by a convergent complex power series $\sum c_\alpha z^\alpha$. Here convergence is the usual convergence of complex power series: on some positive polydisc its absolute majorant is finite at every smaller positive polyradius, as in section 4 of the source. Choose such a smaller $\rho$ with its closed polydisc contained in the representative's neighbourhood. Then $\sum|c_\alpha|\rho^\alpha<\infty$, so $c\in A_\rho$ and its image has exactly the original representative near zero. This proves the union-of-images assertion, without claiming that a single radius represents every germ.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A10_0.pdf, Frenkel exp.10 section 4 printed pp.6-7. Agent-written complete l1 formulation and explicit majorant argument.

proof.text: If $0<\sigma_i\leq\rho_i$, then $\sigma^\alpha\leq\rho^\alpha$ for every $\alpha$. Domination [lem-sfb-absolute-series-domination] applied to the two nonnegative majorants shows that keeping coefficients maps $A_\rho$ into $A_\sigma$ and that $\|c\|_\sigma\leq\|c\|_\rho$. It preserves each coefficient operation, the convolution and the unit. The series evaluations agree on the smaller open polydisc, hence their germs agree. This also covers $\sigma=\rho$.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A10_0.pdf, Frenkel exp.10 section 4 printed pp.6-7. Agent-written complete l1 formulation and explicit majorant argument.

proof.text: Set any chosen coordinates to zero. In the absolutely convergent series every monomial with a positive exponent in one of those coordinates vanishes; every other monomial is unchanged. The remaining coefficient family is in the weighted space for the retained radii, since its weighted absolute sum is a subseries of the original nonnegative majorant, by [lem-wf-summable-family-regrouping]. Restricting that holomorphic representative therefore gives precisely the germ of the retained series. Setting no coordinates to zero is the identity; setting all of them to zero keeps only the constant coefficient.
